binaries.name: capa
binaries.why: Match a binary against capability rules over features extracted from the file and report named capabilities with the features and addresses each match used. A match is a rule-supported hypothesis about what the code can do, not observed behaviour; the rule set and version used are part of the result. The Linux download is pinned to a release and sha256 per architecture; the Homebrew install is unpinned (declared, unverified).

install.apt: pinned download 9.4.0 (install.download): upstream standalone release, whose embedded rules make offline analysis work

binaries.name: floss
binaries.why: Recover strings that plain extraction misses (strings a sample decodes or builds at runtime) by analysis and emulation of its code, without running the sample on a host. Recovery is incomplete and depends on the format, architecture and version; a recovered string is derived, not read at a file offset. Pinned to flare-floss 3.2.0 with its whole dependency set in a hash lock (requires/locks/floss.txt: a wheel hash per architecture where PyPI has one, and the sdist), so the image installs nothing else; a job still records the output of `floss --version`.

binaries.name: olevba
binaries.why: Extract VBA macro source from an Office document and name its auto-execution entry points. An entry-point name shows what a macro declares, not that anything ran. Pinned to oletools 0.60.2 with its whole dependency set in a hash lock (requires/locks/olevba.txt: a wheel hash per architecture where PyPI has one, and the sdist); a job records the version the tool prints.

binaries.name: r2
binaries.why: Disassembly, cross-references and function discovery from the command line, scriptable.

install.apt: pinned download 6.2.2 (install.download): upstream's .deb per architecture; radare2 is not in Debian 12, only in unstable

binaries.name: yara
binaries.why: Match a sample against a rule set and report each match, with the offsets of its string matches where the rule has strings (a condition-only match has none). The pack ships no rules. Unpinned apt package (declared, unverified): the version the image carries is read from the program with `yara --version`.

binaries.name: strings
binaries.why: A first pass over a binary before a parser is chosen. Always search UTF-16LE as well, which strings -el does. Unpinned apt package (declared, unverified): the version the image carries is read from the program.

binaries.name: readelf
binaries.why: Print an ELF file's headers, dynamic section, notes (including the GNU build ID) and symbol tables with GNU binutils, to cross-check pe_info's reading and to read what it does not.

install.brew: brew install binutils (keg-only: readelf is $(brew --prefix binutils)/bin/readelf and is not on PATH)

binaries.licence: GPL-3.0-or-later (the program; binutils as a package mixes licences)

binaries.name: ssdeep
binaries.why: Compute context-triggered piecewise hashes so related binaries can be clustered even when their cryptographic hashes differ. Unpinned apt package (declared, unverified): fuzzy_hash records what `ssdeep -V` printed.

binaries.name: tlsh
binaries.why: Compute and compare Trend Micro Locality Sensitive Hashes for samples with sufficient size and byte diversity. Unpinned apt package (declared, unverified): fuzzy_hash records what `tlsh -version` printed.

install.brew: not available in Homebrew (there is no tlsh formula): build the CLI from the upstream release, or run the tool in the re image, where apt provides tlsh-tools

binaries.name: upx
binaries.why: Test and decompress UPX-compressed executables on a copy, without executing them, preserving the original and recording both hashes. A failure does not show that a file is not packed.

install.apt: pinned download 5.2.1 (install.download): upstream static release per architecture

binaries.name: gcc
binaries.why: Compile a small C program the seat itself writes, in the job's own directory: a scanner over a memory image too large for Python to hold, a decoder for a format no library reads. The source and the build line stay in the record like any other tool. Never a program or a source tree the evidence holds: nothing from the evidence is executed.
binaries.licence: GPL-3.0-or-later with the GCC Runtime Library Exception

binaries.name: make
binaries.why: Build a tool distributed as source, from a tree the operator or a pack supplied; never a source tree the evidence holds.

binaries.name: analyzeHeadless
binaries.why: Ghidra's headless analyzer (support/analyzeHeadless): import a binary into a project kept under $OUT and run its analysis without the GUI, so decompiled functions and cross-references can be read as method, never as a script the evidence supplies. The release is a platform-independent zip (about 570 MB, so the largest download of the image) and needs a 64-bit JDK 21 or later, declared here as `java`. Nothing from the evidence becomes an extension or a script. Pinned to 12.2 (sha256 as the release publishes it).

install.apt: pinned download 12.2 (install.download): upstream's platform-independent zip, which needs the JDK declared as java

binaries.name: java
binaries.why: The 64-bit JDK Ghidra's headless analyzer runs on (analyzeHeadless finds `java` on PATH). Debian 12 carries no JDK 21, so the Eclipse Temurin 21.0.13+9 tarball is pinned per architecture (sha256 as Adoptium publishes it; about 205 MB each).

install.apt: pinned download 21.0.13+9 (install.download): Eclipse Temurin JDK per architecture

binaries.name: diec
binaries.why: Detect It Easy's console program: name the packer, protector, compiler and linker signatures it recognises in a file, as signature matches (a match is a hypothesis, a miss shows nothing). Pinned to 3.21 as upstream's Debian 12 package (sha256 as the release publishes it); upstream publishes no Linux arm64 build, so an arm64 image records it as not installed.

install.apt: pinned download 3.21 (install.download): upstream's .deb for Debian 12 (amd64 only)

binaries.name: dotnet
binaries.why: The .NET runtime a .NET-based decompiler runs on (the framework-dependent ilspycmd build targets net10.0, and is what the arm64 image runs; the amd64 build is Native AOT and needs no runtime). Declared here because the re profile holds no Windows pack and a pack may not depend on another (the same pin the Windows pack declares: 10.0.14, which runs net10.0 programs).

binaries.name: ilspycmd
binaries.why: Decompile a .NET assembly to C# with the ILSpy command line, as a reconstruction written to a file (clr_inspect, in a job run as secret output). A decompiler's output is an interpretation of the IL, not the author's source. Pinned to 11.2.0.10050 from nuget.org: the amd64 image takes the Native AOT platform package ilspycmd.linux-x64 (no runtime needed), the arm64 image the framework-dependent package ilspycmd.any, run by the .NET runtime declared above; neither package has a NuGet dependency. Each package is checked against its sha256 and unpacked whole by images/install.py (nupkg rules). The pointer package ilspycmd, which holds no program, is not used. The program was not run for real by the change that declared it (no .NET on the machine that wrote it); a job records the output of `ilspycmd --version`.

install.brew: dotnet tool install --global ilspycmd (needs the .NET SDK 10 or newer; unpinned, declared and unverified)
install.apt: pinned download 11.2.0.10050 (install.download): the NuGet platform package per architecture, unpacked by install.py; arm64 is run by the .NET runtime (dotnet)

binaries.name: qpdf
binaries.why: A second reader of a PDF's structure: check and list its objects, streams and encryption with a parser that is not this pack's own, so the two readings can be compared. Debian 12 carries qpdf 11.3.0; upstream's 12.4.2 release binaries are not pinned because their layout cannot be checked without fetching them. The apt snapshot date pins the version.

binaries.name: osslsigncode
binaries.why: Verify an Authenticode signature with OpenSSL (`osslsigncode verify`) instead of handwritten cryptography, from trust material the case supplies. Upstream publishes source and Windows/macOS builds only, so the Debian 12 package (2.5) is declared; the apt snapshot date pins the version.
binaries.licence: GPL-3.0-or-later with an OpenSSL linking exception (upstream's COPYING; GitHub does not machine-read it)
